# Maintained Readium integration

Upstream: Readium Swift Toolkit 3.11.0, revision d82f44f4f05d87add9e22a8b75abbd61dce745dd, BSD-3-Clause (LICENSE).
This is XianxiaReader's explicitly maintained local extension, NOT an official merged release.

Only Shared, Streamer, Navigator and Internal sources/resources are included. The manifest retains upstream remote dependency constraints but excludes unused products/test publications. Navigator preference integration is adapted from Eugene Martinson / emartinson's PR811 (https://github.com/readium/swift-toolkit/pull/811); the whole-book placeholder implementation is replaced by XianxiaReader's bounded fixed-viewport resource window.

UPSTREAM.json records SHA-256 of original Git blob contents and explicitly changed files. Original Swift contents were verified against the pristine 3.11 Git revision during recovery. Validate with scripts/check_repository.py. Source modifications require a reviewed provenance update and full iOS CI; never patch SourcePackages caches. Original binary assets and DOM scripts remain unchanged. Copyright notices and binary ThirdPartyNotices are retained.

The root lock is the untouched resolver artifact from macOS run38496501326. Six retained remote pins match the previous official-package lock; the unused server/SQLite/LCP dependency graph was pruned by SwiftPM. Removed pins and resolution evidence remain in UPSTREAM.json. Every subsequent resolve/test/build must use the genuine lock strictly; first-resolution bootstrap is off.

Continuous locators retain original href/progression/position/text and use the HTML Locator DOMRange extension for character anchors. xianxiaContinuousAnchorVersion=1 and xianxiaViewportOffset preserve the character's local viewport displacement. Only marked continuous save locators receive this precise restore override; incoming search hits keep upstream text matching. Delayed layout results must match the resource epoch and viewport revision. Explicit shutdown clears pending loads and WebKit message handlers.

Continuous mode currently targets horizontal LTR reflowable EPUB. Fixed layout, RTL and vertical writing retain the original paths. The stable paginated/chapter-scrolling implementations and SearchService API remain available. Verify real two-resource boundaries, reverse movement, DOM locator restoration, reflow anchor stability and resource bounds before shipping.

M4 appearance extension dispatches the existing Navigator runScript scopes to the bounded continuous viewport's loaded/current/resource spread views. Previously only paged views received dynamic CSS preferences. Current resource is updated first, retained views are bounded, and a replaced continuous viewport rejects remaining work. Preferences and resource caching still use the original 3.11 API; no dependency or lock changes.

Build16 reflow recovery uses the ViewModel's existing needsInvalidation decision for paginated typography. Injected CSS/cache update and a pagination rebuild are exclusive with dynamic CSS scripts, following upstream's mode/layout invalidation contract. This prevents queued typography writes from reaching replacement pages after DOM anchor restoration. Color-only changes and continuous mode retain dynamic CSS. Bounded numeric/boolean lifecycle diagnostics and a real WebKit counter regression distinguish the paths; the original nonzero text/180-percent/reopen regression remains intact.

Build17 paged location notifications for horizontal LTR reflowable text combine the existing bounded DOM anchor sampler with upstream progression metadata. This prevents ordinary page notifications from erasing the precise typography anchor before close/reopen. Current spread, offset, viewport and location revision guard awaited work; fixed/RTL/vertical paths keep upstream behavior. Existing nonzero-character/180-percent/reopen assertions remain, with an additional full-anchor assertion before reopen. This is separate from the withdrawn native-scroll callback experiment.
